_comment: RECORDING POLICY. Identical to meridian.json except risky_action_handling,
which is 'flag' rather than 'require_confirmation'.
Why this file exists, and why it is not a hole. Recording an irreversible
capability requires performing the irreversible action exactly once: you
cannot record a review->post flow without posting, and a gate that blocks
discovery makes every capability ending in a post unrecordable. So the gate
is relaxed for recording, by an engineer, on the command line, in a named
file that says so -- and the run's evidence records which policy it used.
That is the opposite of the bug this replaced. Until phase 2, discovery
never evaluated step risk at all: the executor's gate read Step.risk and
discovery built every Step without one, so the gate could not fire and
nobody knew. The difference between 'the gate is off because of a bug' and
'the gate is off because this file says so' is the whole distinction.
The emitted artifact does NOT inherit this. discovery/recorder.py always
writes risky_action_handling: 'require_confirmation' into the capability,
so a relaxed recording session cannot produce something that posts
unattended in replay.
Use meridian.json for anything that is not recording a known-irreversible
flow. If you reach for this file, you should be able to say which step you
expect to perform and why.
